text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Foreign Ministry expressed concern about the safety of the country's residents travelling to Poland following the killing of a Latvian tourist in an armed robbery last week.

- Riga harbour board ordered its management to end its involvement in the company LNT Riga, a local rival of Statoil and Neste in building of petroleum terminal. LNT recently signed a contract with the port, causing protests from the foreign oil companies, which said it was a violation of erlier agreements.

- President Ulmanis invited all political parties to an open discussion on moral principles in politics, following media reports on a minister in the current cabinet being involved in Soviet dissident trials.
- German experts confirmed suspicions about Kreutzfeld- Jakob's disease being the cause of the death of a Latvian woman earlier this year.
- The government approved rules introducing a departure tax at Riga airport.
- Leading bank Unibanka announced audited 1996 results with the bank's profit having doubled to 6 million lats against the previous year and the profit per share was 34 santimes.
- Union Baltic Bank in Riga has become an international subsidiary of the Latvian Savings Bank, which took over all the assets and liabilities of the bank in a merger.

- The cabinet approved Latvia's accession to the Council of Europe Convention on Human Rights and five additional protocols of the Convention. The sixth protocol, which provides for the abolition of the death penalty, will not be signed far the time being.

- The Dienas Bizness editor-in-chief submitted a draft law on "national reconciliation" to parliament, which aims at ending discrimination against former Communist Party and KGB workers expect for those accused of crimes against humanity.
- The turnover of Ventspils Nafta oil terminal in February amounted to 2.13 million tonnes of oil and oil products, 199,000 tonne increase in comparison to a year ago.
